akhfash:5-5.t: He said ﴿ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ﴾, i.e. by reckoning, and He implied the khabar (predicate). I think — and Allah knows best — that He meant "they run by reckoning".

akhfash:11-11.t: And He said ﴿ذَاتُ ٱلأَكْمَامِ﴾: its singular is "الكِمُّ" (sheath).

akhfash:48-48.t: And He said ﴿ذَوَاتَآ أَفْنَانٍ﴾: its singular is "الفَنَنُ" (branch).

akhfash:64-64.t: And He said ﴿مُدْهَآمَّتَانِ﴾, as you say "اِزْوَرَّ" and "اِزْوارَّ" (to turn aside).

daas-irab:68-68.t: ﴿فِيهِما﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿فاكِهَةٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ﴾ both conjoined to what precedes them; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:70-70.t: ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿خَيْراتٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿حِسانٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of خيرات; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:72-72.t: ﴿حُورٌ﴾ a badal (substitute) from خيرات. ﴿مَقْصُوراتٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of حور. ﴿فِي الْخِيامِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) مقصورات; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:76-76.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿عَلى رَفْرَفٍ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them. ﴿خُضْرٍ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of رفرف. ﴿وَعَبْقَرِيٍّ﴾ conjoined to رفرف. ﴿حِسانٍ﴾ a ṣifa of عبقري.

daas-irab:78-78.t: ﴿تَبارَكَ اسْمُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ذِي﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of ربك, and it is muḍāf. ﴿الْجَلالِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْإِكْرامِ﴾ conjoined to الجلال; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:1-4.t: ﴿الرَّحْمنُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿خَلَقَ الْإِنْسانَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is a second khabar. ﴿عَلَّمَهُ الْبَيانَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil is latent; البيان is its second mafʿūl; the clause is a third khabar.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿الشَّمْسُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَالْقَمَرُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. ﴿بِحُسْبانٍ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وَالنَّجْمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَالشَّجَرُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. ﴿يَسْجُدانِ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the alif is its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَالسَّماءَ﴾ a conjunction, and mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned. ﴿رَفَعَها﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) and has no grammatical position, and the implied clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزانَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿أَلَّا﴾ an is a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative, and lā is negating. ﴿تَطْغَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿فِي الْمِيزانِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; an and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by an implied preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to وضع.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْوَزْنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا تُخْسِرُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الْمِيزانَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned; the implied clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَضَعَها﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لِلْأَنامِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿فِيها﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿فاكِهَةٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَالنَّخْلُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to فاكهة. ﴿ذاتُ﴾ an adjective. ﴿الْأَكْمامِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَالْحَبُّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to فاكهة. ﴿ذُو﴾ an adjective. ﴿الْعَصْفِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالرَّيْحانُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and بأي: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تكذبان. ﴿آلاءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿رَبِّكُما﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿تُكَذِّبانِ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the alif is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿خَلَقَ الْإِنْسانَ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ صَلْصالٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿كَالْفَخَّارِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted adjective of صلصال.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿وَخَلَقَ الْجَانَّ مِنْ مارِجٍ﴾ its i'rab is like the preceding one. ﴿مِنْ نارٍ﴾ an adjective of مارج; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿رَبُّ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), annexed to المشرقين. ﴿الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَرَبُّ الْمَغْرِبَيْنِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl (object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَلْتَقِيانِ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the alif is its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿بَيْنَهُما بَرْزَخٌ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate) and a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿لا﴾ negating; and ﴿يَبْغِيانِ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the alif is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿يَخْرُجُ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْهُمَا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿اللُّؤْلُؤُ﴾ fāʿil (agent), nominative. ﴿وَالْمَرْجانُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to اللؤلؤ; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿الْجَوارِ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿الْمُنْشَآتُ﴾ an adjective of الجوار. ﴿فِي الْبَحْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) المنشئات. ﴿كَالْأَعْلامِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿كُلُّ مَنْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) annexed to the relative noun, and the relative noun is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿فانٍ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, it being a defective noun (ism manqūṣ); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿وَيَبْقى وَجْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ذُو﴾ an adjective of وجه, in construct (muḍāf). ﴿الْجَلالِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْإِكْرامِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الجلال; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿يَسْئَلُهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl (object). ﴿مَنْ﴾ its fāʿil (agent). ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السموات; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿كُلَّ﴾ an adverb, in construct (muḍāf). ﴿يَوْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي شَأْنٍ﴾ khabar (predicate).

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿سَنَفْرُغُ﴾ the sīn is for futurity, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَيُّهَ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda). ﴿الثَّقَلانِ﴾ badal (substitute); the vocative clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:33-33.t: ﴿يا مَعْشَرَ﴾ a vocative (munādā) in construct. ﴿الْجِنِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالْإِنْسِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ﴾ in is a conditional particle, and a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْ تَنْفُذُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and what follows it is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of استطعتم. ﴿مِنْ أَقْطارِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات. ﴿فَانْفُذُوا﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿تَنْفُذُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿بِسُلْطانٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb.

daas-irab:35-35.t: ﴿يُرْسَلُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿عَلَيْكُما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿شُواظٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ نارٍ﴾ an adjective of شواظ. ﴿وَنُحاسٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to شواظ. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and lā is negating. ﴿تَنْتَصِرانِ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the alif is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:37-37.t: ﴿فَإِذَا﴾ the fāʾ is a particle of resumption, and idhā is an adverbial conditional particle not governing the jussive. ﴿انْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فَكانَتْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir). ﴿وَرْدَةً﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَالدِّهانِ﴾ an adjective of وردة.

daas-irab:39-39.t: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and يومئذ is an adverb of time annexed to idh. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿يُسْئَلُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿إِنْسٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the verbal clause is the apodosis. ﴿وَلا جَانٌّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to إنس.

daas-irab:41-41.t: ﴿يُعْرَفُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِسِيماهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿فَيُؤْخَذُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿بِالنَّواصِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun standing in the place of the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿وَالْأَقْدامِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to النواصي; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:43-43.t: ﴿هذِهِ جَهَنَّمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an omitted saying. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective of جهنم. ﴿يُكَذِّبُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿بِهَا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾ fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:44-44.t: ﴿يَطُوفُونَ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بَيْنَها﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿وَبَيْنَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to بينها. ﴿حَمِيمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿آنٍ﴾ an adjective of حميم, genitive (majrūr) by the implied (muqaddar) kasra on the omitted yāʾ.

daas-irab:46-46.t: ﴿وَلِمَنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿خافَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿مَقامَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رَبِّهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿جَنَّتانِ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of man, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:48-48.t: ﴿ذَواتا﴾ an adjective of جنتان. ﴿أَفْنانٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:50-50.t: ﴿فِيهِما﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿عَيْنانِ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause has no grammatical position. ﴿تَجْرِيانِ﴾ a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and the alif is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is an adjective of عينان.

daas-irab:51-51.t: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ﴾ its i'rab has preceded.

daas-irab:52-52.t: ﴿فِيهِما﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فاكِهَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿زَوْجانِ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:54-54.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ. ﴿عَلى فُرُشٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them. ﴿بَطائِنُها﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is an adjective of فرش. ﴿وَجَنَى﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ in construct (muḍāf). ﴿الْجَنَّتَيْنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿دانٍ﴾ khabar; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:56-56.t: ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿قاصِراتُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), in construct (muḍāf). ﴿الطَّرْفِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl (object). ﴿إِنْسٌ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قَبْلَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿وَلا جَانٌّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to إنس.

daas-irab:58-58.t: ﴿كَأَنَّهُنَّ﴾ kaʾanna and its noun. ﴿الْياقُوتُ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿وَالْمَرْجانُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الياقوت; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:60-60.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾ a particle of interrogation. ﴿جَزاءُ الْإِحْسانِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) annexed to الإحسان. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿الْإِحْسانِ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source vowels the khabar with kasra (الْإِحْسانِ); as khabar the Quranic word is الْإِحْسانُ.]

daas-irab:62-62.t: ﴿وَمِنْ دُونِهِما﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿جَنَّتانِ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:66-66.t: [Translator's note: the source text of this entry is garbled: the quotation brackets and first letters of the Quranic words are lost (it reads «ِيهِما», «يْنانِ», «ضَّاخَتانِ»). The words are restored below from the verse, ﴿فِيهِما عَيْنانِ نَضَّاخَتانِ﴾.] ﴿فِيهِما﴾ an advanced khabar (predicate). ﴿عَيْنانِ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿نَضَّاخَتانِ﴾ an adjective of عينان; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

farraa:5-5.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿بِحُسْبَانٍ﴾. A reckoning and stations [188/ب] for the sun and the moon, which they do not exceed.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلنَّجْمُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدَانِ﴾. «النجم» is what sprouts (najama), such as grass, herbs and the like; and «الشجر» is what stands on a trunk. Then He said «يسجدان» (the two prostrate); their prostration is that they face the sun when it rises, then incline with it until the shade turns. When the Arabs combine two plural (collective) nouns of things other than people, such as lote-trees and palm trees, they make their verb singular, saying: «الشاء والنعم قد أقبل» (the sheep and the cattle have come), and «النخل والسدر قد ارتوى» (the palms and the lote-trees have been watered). This is most of their speech, and putting it in the dual is permissible.
Al-Kisāʾī said: I heard the Arabs say: «مرت بنا غنمان سودان» and «سود» (two black flocks passed by us).
Al-Farrāʾ said: «سود» is better than «سودان», because it is an adjective that applies to the two. When one of the two is feminine, such as sheep and camels, they say: «الشاء والإبل مقبلة» (the sheep and the camels are coming), because «الشاء» is masculine and «الإبل» feminine. Had you said «مقبلان» it would be permissible; and had you said «مقبلتان», taking «الشاء» as feminine along with the feminine of «الإبل», it would be correct; but the singular is more frequent and better.
When you say «هؤلاء قومك وإبلهم قد أقبلوا» (these are your people and their camels, they have come), the verb is taken to refer to the people specifically, because the action is theirs, and they are the ones who bring the camels. Had you meant the coming of both these and those, «قد أقبلوا» would (still) be permissible, because when people are mixed with some animals, their action becomes like the action of people, as He said: ﴿وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ المَاءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, and the she-camel became like people.
Of this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِى عَلَى بَطْنِهِ﴾; «مَنْ» is only used for people, but when He detailed them, having gathered them together in His saying ﴿وَاللهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ دَابّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ﴾, He detailed them in the manner used for people.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا...﴾ above the earth; ﴿وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ﴾: in the earth, and it is justice.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «وخَفْض الميزان»; «الخفض» (lowering) and «الوضع» (setting down) are close in meaning.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلاَّ تَطْغَوْاْ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «لا تطغوا» without «أن», «فى الوزن وأقيموا اللسان».
And His saying: ﴿أَلاَّ تَطْغَوْاْ﴾: if you wish, you make it jussive (majzūm) with the intent of prohibition; and if you wish, you make it accusative (manṣūb) by «أن», as Allah said: ﴿إِنِّى أمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَلا تَكونَنَّ﴾. That (تطغوا) should be in the position of a jussive is dearer to me, because after it comes an imperative.

farraa:9-10.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ﴾.
﴿وَٱلأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلأَنَامِ﴾: for all creatures.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْحَبُّ ذُو ٱلْعَصْفِ وَٱلرَّيْحَانُ﴾. Al-Aʿmash read it in the genitive, and the people read it in the nominative.
Whoever read it in the genitive meant: «ذو العصف وذو الريحان» (possessing husk and possessing fragrance/sustenance); whoever read «الريحان» in the nominative made it follow «ذو». «العصف», according to what they mentioned, is the green leaf of the crop; for the Arabs say «خرجنا نعصف الزرع» (we went out to cut the crop) when they cut some of it before it ripens; that is «العصف». «الريحان» is its sustenance, and «الحب» is what is eaten of it. «الريحان» in the speech of the Arabs means sustenance; they say «خرجنا نطلب ريحان الله» (we went out seeking Allah's rayḥān), sustenance in their usage. Some of them said: «ذو العصف» is what is eaten of the grain, and «الريحان» is the sound part that has not been eaten.
Had a reader read: "والحبّ ذا العصف والريحانَ", it would have been permissible, that is: He created this and this. In the codices of the people of Syria it is «والحبّ ذا العصف», but we have not heard any reader read it so; just as in some codices of the people of Kufa there is ﴿والجار ذا القربى﴾ [189/ا] and no one has read it so. Sometimes a word is written in one way while it is read in (various) ways.
It has reached me that the letter of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, was written: «هذا كتاب من على بن أبو طالب» — its scribes wrote «أبو» in all cases — and it is declined in speech when it is read aloud.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿فَبِأَيِّ آلاۤءِ رَبِّكُمَا تُكَذِّبَانِ﴾. At the beginning of the passage He only mentioned «الإنسان» (man); there are two explanations of this. The first: the Arabs address (a single person) with the dual form of the verb; one says: «ارحلاها، ازجراها يا غلام» (saddle her, drive her on, boy!).
The other explanation: the mention was intended of mankind and the jinn, so it runs for both of them from the beginning of the sura to its end.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿خَلَقَ ٱلإِنسَانَ مِن صَلْصَالٍ كَٱلْفَخَّارِ﴾.
It is clay mixed with sand, which rings (ṣalṣala) as pottery rings. It is also said: from stinking «صلصال», by which they mean «صلّ» (it went putrid); then «صلصال» is said, just as one says «صرّ الباب» (the door creaked) when closing, and «صرصر». The Arabs repeat (in place of) the lām (the third radical) in the doubled (verb), so it is said «كركرت الرجلَ», meaning «كررْته» (I turned him back), and «كبكبته», meaning «كببته» (I threw him on his face).
I heard one of the Arabs say: «أتيت فلانا فبشبش بى» (I came to so-and-so and he welcomed me), from «البشاشة» (cheerfulness). They only did this out of dislike for three letters of one kind coming together.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿مِن مَّارِجٍ مِّن نَّارٍ﴾.
«المارج» is a fire below the veil — according to what al-Kalbī mentioned — from which these thunderbolts come, and the skin of the sky is seen from it.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿رَبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَرَبُّ ٱلْمَغْرِبَيْنِ﴾.
The readers agreed on its nominative; had it been put in the genitive — that is, in its inflection — following His saying «فبأى آلاء ربكما»: «ربِّ المشرقين», it would have been correct.
The two easts are the rising-place of winter and the rising-place of summer; likewise the two wests.

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿مَرَجَ ٱلْبَحْرَيْنِ﴾. He is saying: He let them loose, then they meet afterwards.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخٌ﴾.
A barrier; «لا يبغيان»: the fresh does not encroach on the salt so that both become fresh, and the salt does not encroach on the fresh so that both become salt.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا الُّلؤْلُؤُ وَالمَرْجَانُ﴾.
It only comes out of the salt, not the fresh. «اللؤلؤ» is the large (pearls), and «المرجان» is the small pearls.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَهُ ٱلْجَوَارِ ٱلْمُنشَئَاتُ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read (المنشِئات) with a kasra on the shīn, making them the ones that come and go (of themselves). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd it is (المنشآت), and so read al-Ḥasan and the people of the Hijaz, with a fatḥa on the shīn, making them acted upon: they are made to come and made to go.
And His saying: ﴿كَٱلأَعْلاَمِ﴾.
Like mountains: He likened the ship to a mountain; and every mountain, when it is tall, is a «عَلَم».

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلْجَلاَلِ﴾.
This one, and the one at the end of it with «ذى» — both of them in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh are «ذى» — are genitive in inflection, because they are part of the description of «ربك», Blessed and Exalted. In our reading it is: ﴿وَيَبْقَىٰ وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو ٱلْجَلاَلِ وَٱلإِكْرَامِ﴾, [ذو] being part of the description of «وجه» of our Lord, Blessed and Exalted.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿كُلَّ يَوْمٍ هُوَ فِي شَأْنٍ﴾, without hamza.
He said: I asked al-Farrāʾ [189/ب] about (شان), and he said: I pronounce it with hamza throughout the Quran except in Sūrat al-Raḥmān, because it is among verses that are without hamza. His affair (shaʾn) every day is that He causes one to die and one to be born, enriches this one and impoverishes that one, among countless deeds.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ أَيُّهَ ٱلثَّقَلاَنِ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Abū Isrāʾīl told me: I heard Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read: "سَيَفْرغُ لكم", and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb likewise; and the readers after that: "سَنَفْرُغُ لكم"; and some of them read "سيُفرغ لكم".
This is a threat from Allah, for He, Mighty and Majestic, is not distracted by one thing from another. You say to a man who has no occupation: «قد فرغت لى، قد فرغت لشتمى» (you have made yourself free for me, for insulting me), that is: you have set about it and turned to it.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰمَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنسِ إِنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَن تَنفُذُواْ﴾.
He did not say «إن استطعتما» (dual); had it been so, it would have been correct, just as He said (يُرسل عليكما) and did not say «عليكم»: «شُواظ من نار ونحاس فلا تنتصران». He used the dual in «عليكما» and «تنتصران» according to the wording, and the plural according to the meaning. «النحاس» is nominative; had it been genitive it would have been correct, meaning: of fire and of «نحاس».
«الشواظ» is pure fire, and «النحاس» is smoke. One of them recited to me:
يضىء كضوء سراج السلي * ط لم يجعل الله منه نحاسا
(It shines like the light of a lamp of salīṭ, from which Allah made no smoke.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: a Bedouin of Banū Sulaym told me: «السليط» is the fat of the camel's hump, and it gives no smoke when used in a lamp.
And I heard that it is «الخَلّ», which is sesame oil; and I heard that it is olive oil. Olive oil is more correct, in my view.
Al-Ḥasan read (شِواظ) with a kasra on the shīn, just as one says of a herd of wild cattle «صِوار» and «صُوَار».

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا ٱنشَقَّتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَكَانَتْ وَرْدَةً كَٱلدِّهَانِ﴾.
By «الوردة» He meant the (bay) horse: the bay mare in spring is a bay inclining to yellow; when the cold becomes severe she is a red bay; and after that she is a bay inclining to dust-colour. So He likened the changing colour of the sky to the changing colour of the bay among horses, and the bay in the variety of its colours was likened to oil (duhn) and the variety of its colours.
And it is said that «الدهان» is red leather.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لاَّ يُسْأَلُ عَن ذَنبِهِ إِنسٌ وَلاَ جَآنٌّ﴾.
The meaning is: no human will be asked about his sin, nor jinn about his sin, because they will be known by their marks, as Allah described: the disbeliever will be known by the blackness of his face and the blueness of his eye, and the believer will be radiant on the forehead and limbs from the traces of his ablution.
«[Translator's note: «رزقة» is as printed, evidently for «زرقة» (blueness).]»

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذِهِ جَهَنَّمُ ٱلَّتِي يُكَذِّبُ بِهَا ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: «هذه جهنم التى كنتما بها تكذبان، تَصليانها لا تموتان فيها ولا تحييان تطوفان» (This is Hell which you two used to deny; you two will burn in it, neither dying nor living in it, going round).

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَهَا﴾.
Between the punishment of Hell and the boiling water when they are thirsty. «الآنى» is that whose heat has reached its utmost intensity.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلِمَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتَانِ﴾.
The exegetes mentioned that they are two orchards among the orchards of Paradise. It may also be, in Arabic, a single garden which the Arabs put in the dual in their poetry. One of them recited to me:
ومَهْمَين قَذَفَين مَرْتَين * قطعته [بالأََمِّ] لا بالسَّمْتين
(Many a pair of far, bare, waterless deserts I have crossed by the straight course, not by the two tracks.)
He means a single desert and a single track. Another recited to me:
يسعى بكيداء ولهذمين * قد جعل الأرطاة جنتين
(He hastens with a bow and two arrowheads; he has made the arṭā shrub into two gardens.)
That is because poetry has rhymes which addition and reduction set right, so it tolerates what (ordinary) speech does not tolerate.
Al-Farrāʾ said: «الكيداء» is the bow. One says «لهذِم» and «لهذَم», two dialectal forms; it is the arrow(head).

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَى فُرُشٍ بَطَآئِنُهَا مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ﴾. «الإستبرق» is the thick kind of brocade. The lining (biṭāna) may be the outer side (ẓihāra), and the outer side the lining, in the speech of the Arabs; that is because each of them [190/ا] may be a face. The Arabs say «this is the back (ẓahr) of the sky» and «this is the belly (baṭn) of the sky» for its outer side that you see.
He said: one of the eloquent ḥadīth transmitters told me, from Ibn al-Zubayr, who was censuring the killers of ʿUthmān, may Allah have mercy on him, and said: they came out against him like thieves from behind the village; so Allah killed them every kind of killing, and those of them who escaped escaped beneath the bellies of the stars.
He means: they fled by night. So he made the backs of the stars their bellies; and that is permissible according to what I have told you.

farraa:56-56.t:
His saying: ﴿لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ [إِنسٌ]﴾.
All the readers read «يطمثهن» with a kasra on the mīm. Al-Farrāʾ told us: a man told me, from Abū Isḥāq, who said: I used to pray behind the companions of ʿAlī and the companions of ʿAbd Allāh, and I heard them read (لم يطمُثهن) with a ḍamma on the mīm. Al-Kisāʾī used to read one (occurrence) with a ḍamma on the mīm and the other with a kasra on the mīm, so as not to depart from these two reports. «لم يطمِثهن» means: they have not deflowered them. (He said: «طمثها» means: he had intercourse with her; and that is because of the blood.)

farraa:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿مُدْهَآمَّتَانِ﴾: He is saying: green inclining to black, from (abundant) watering.

farraa:68-68.t:
His saying: ﴿فِيهِمَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ﴾.
Some of the exegetes say: neither pomegranates nor palms are fruit. They have taken a position, but the Arabs count those as fruit.
If you ask: then how are palms and pomegranates mentioned again if they are among the fruit? I say: that is like His saying: ﴿حَافِظُوا على الصَّلواتِ والصلاةِ الوُسْطَى﴾. He commanded them to guard all the prayers, then mentioned the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr) again to emphasise it. Likewise palms and pomegranates were mentioned again to make the people of Paradise desire them. Similar is His saying in al-Ḥajj: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَنْ فِى السَّمَاواتِ وَمَنْ فِى الأَرْضِ﴾, then He said: ﴿وكَثيرٌ مِّن الناسِ، وكثيرٌ حَقَّ عليه الْعَذابُ﴾, though He had mentioned them at the beginning of the statement in His saying ﴿مَنْ فِى السّماواتِ ومَن فِى الأرضِ﴾. Some of the exegetes said: by His saying ﴿مَنْ فِى السماواتِ ومن فى الأرضِ﴾ He only meant the angels, then He mentioned people after them.

farraa:70-70.t:
His saying: ﴿فِيهِنَّ خَيْرَاتٌ حِسَانٌ﴾.
It refers back to the four gardens — two gardens and two gardens — so He said «فيهن». The Arabs say: «أعطنى الخَيْرَة منهن», «الخِيرة منهن» and «الخيّرة منهن» (give me the best of them). Had a reader read «الخَيراتُ» or «الخيرات», both would have been correct.
«[Translator's note: the two variants are printed without distinguishing vowels; presumably «خَيْرات» and «خَيِّرات» are meant.]»

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿حُورٌ مَّقْصُورَاتٌ﴾.
They are restricted to their husbands, that is, kept (for them), so that they want no others and do not look to anyone else. The Arabs call the curtained bridal canopy «المقصورة» and «القصورة», and they call a secluded woman «قصورة». The poet said:
لعمرى لقد حببِت كلَّ قَصورة * إلىّ وما تدرى بذاك القصائر
عَنَيْتُ قصوراتِ الحجال ولم أرِد * قصارَ الخُطا، شرُّ النساء البحاتر
(By my life, you have made every secluded woman dear to me, though the secluded ones do not know it. I meant those secluded in canopies, not the short-stepped; the worst of women are the stumpy.)
«البحاتر» and «البهاتر» both mean the short (women); a man is called «بحتر», «بحترى», «بحترة» and «بحترية».

farraa:76-76.t:
His saying: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَىٰ رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ﴾.
They mentioned that these are the meadows of Paradise; and some of them said: they are cushions. ﴿وَعَبْقَرِيٍّ حِسَانٍ﴾: thick carpets.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us: Muḥammad told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us: Muʿādh ibn Muslim ibn Abī Sāda told me: Your neighbour [190/ب] Zuhayr al-Qurqubī used to read: «متكئين على رفارف خضر وعباقرى حسان».
He said: «الرفارف» may be correct; but «العباقرى» not, because the alif of the (broken) plural is not followed by four letters, nor by three sound letters.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Raḥmān
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الرَّحْمَنُ﴾ ﴿عَلَّمَ القُرْآنَ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 2]: "اَلرَّحْمَنُ" is one of the names of Allah the Exalted; it is not said of anyone other than Him. It is in the earlier scriptures, and its meaning is: the One abundant in mercy.

zajjaj:10-10.t: And His saying: ﴿والأرْضَ وضَعَها لِلأنامِ﴾: "اَلْأنامُ" means humans and jinn.

zajjaj:11-11.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيها فاكِهَةٌ والنَّخْلُ ذاتُ الأكْمامِ﴾: the meaning of ﴿الأكْمامِ﴾ is: that which covers. Every tree that puts forth something sheathed has akmām (sheaths). The akmām of the palm tree are what cover its heart (jummār) of fronds, fibre and trunk; and everything the palm tree puts forth has sheaths: the spathe's sheath (kumm) is its husk. From this the cap is called "kumma", because it covers the head, and from this come "the two sleeves (kummā) of the shirt", because they cover the hands.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والحَبُّ ذُو العَصْفِ والرَّيْحانُ﴾, and it is also read "والرَّيْحانَ", but the majority reading is ﴿والرَّيْحانُ﴾. Al-ʿaṣf is the leaves of the crop; it is also said that straw is al-ʿaṣf, and one also says al-ʿaṣfa. The poet said:
؎تَسْقِي مَذانِبَ قَدْ مالَتْ عَصِيفَتُها ∗∗∗ آتِيُّها مِن أتِيِّ الماءِ مَطْمُومُ
(It waters channels whose blades of crop have bent over; their inflow is brimming from the inflowing water.)
It is also transmitted "بِأتِيِّ الماءِ". The meaning of ﴿ذُو العَصْفِ والرَّيْحانُ﴾ is: having leaves and provision. The Arabs say "subḥāna llāhi wa-rayḥānahu", and the philologists said its meaning is "and [I seek] His provision". Al-Namir ibn Tawlab said:
؎سَلامُ الإلَهِ ورَيْحانُهُ ∗∗∗ ورَحْمَتُهُ وسَماءٌ دُرَرْ
(The peace of God and His rayḥān, His mercy, and a sky pouring abundantly.)
He said: the meaning of "رَيْحانُهُ" is His provision. Whoever reads "والرَّيْحانِ" «[Translator's note: the source here has the genitive, whereas the variant cited above was written with the accusative, والرَّيْحانَ.]» conjoins it to "اَلْعَصْفِ"; and whoever reads ﴿والرَّيْحانُ﴾ conjoins it to ﴿الحَبِّ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 95] «[Translator's note: so in the printed text; the reference is to الحَبُّ in this verse, al-Raḥmān: 12.]». The meaning would then be: "In them both there is fruit; in them both are grain with husks; and in them both is rayḥān." So "اَلرَّيْحانُ" here would be the fragrant plant that is smelled, and it may also here be provision.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioned in this surah what indicates His oneness: the creation of man, the teaching of clear speech, and the creation of the sun, the moon, the sky and the earth. Then He addressed humans and jinn, saying: "فَبِأيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ", that is: which of the favours of your Lord, among these things mentioned, do you both deny? For all of them are favours bestowed upon you, in their guiding you to His oneness, and in His providing you with what sustains you and is the means to your life. "اَلْآلاءُ": its singular is "ألًى" and "إلًى". And everywhere in the surah that His saying "فَبِأيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ" occurs, its meaning is as we have explained: So which of the favours of your Lord do you both deny?!

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَلَقَ الإنْسانَ مِن صَلْصالٍ كالفَخّارِ﴾. And He said elsewhere: ﴿إنّا خَلَقْناهم مِن طِينٍ لازِبٍ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 11], and He said: ﴿مِن حَمَإٍ مَسْنُونٍ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 26], and He said: ﴿إنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسى عِنْدَ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ خَلَقَهُ مِن تُرابٍ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 59]. These expressions from which Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said that He created man differ in wording, but in meaning they go back to a single origin, for the origin of clay is dust. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He created Adam from dust, which was made into clay, then it changed and became like black mud, then it changed and became ṣalṣāl like pottery — ṣalṣāl being the dry [clay]. All of this has dust as its origin, and there is nothing in it that contradicts any other part. We have explained this only because a group of heretics ask about the like of this in order to confuse the weak. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known from what He created the father of all humans, Adam, peace be upon him, and made known from what He created the origin of the jinn, saying: ﴿وَخَلَقَ الجانَّ مِن مارِجٍ مِن نارٍ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 15]. "اَلْمارِجُ" is the flame mixed with the blackness of the fire.

zajjaj:17-17.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَبُّ المَشْرِقَيْنِ ورَبُّ المَغْرِبَيْنِ﴾: by this He means the two rising-places of the sun, and likewise the moon, and the two setting-places of the sun and the moon. One of the two rising-places is the rising-place of winter and the other the rising-place of summer, and likewise the two setting-places.

zajjaj:19-19.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَرَجَ البَحْرَيْنِ يَلْتَقِيانِ﴾: the meaning of "مَرَجَ" is: He mixed; meaning the salt sea and the fresh sea. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿بَيْنَهُما بَرْزَخٌ لا يَبْغِيانِ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 20]: "اَلْبَرْزَخُ" is the barrier, and it is a barrier from the power of Allah. "لا يَبْغِيانِ": the salt does not encroach upon the fresh so as to mix with it, nor the fresh upon the salt so as to mix with it.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying: ﴿عَلَّمَ القُرْآنَ﴾: its meaning is: He made it easy to be remembered.

zajjaj:22-22.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنهُما اللُّؤْلُؤُ والمَرْجانُ﴾: "اَلْمَرْجانُ" is small pearls, and "اَللُّؤْلُؤُ" is a comprehensive name for the beads that come out of the sea. He said ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنهُما﴾ (comes out of them both) although it comes out only of the salt sea, because He had mentioned them both and joined them together; so if it comes out of one of them, it has come out of them both. Similar to this is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ طِباقًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 15] ﴿وَجَعَلَ القَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِراجًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 16], while the sun is in the lowest heaven; but since He mentioned the seven collectively, what is in one of them is in them. It is also read "يُخْرَجُ مِنهُما" (is brought out of them both), with ḍamma on the yāʾ.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَهُ الجَوارِ المُنْشَآتُ في البَحْرِ كالأعْلامِ﴾: "اَلْجَوارِي" — the pause on it is with the yāʾ; the yāʾ dropped in pronunciation only because of the quiescence of the lām «[Translator's note: i.e. the lām of the following article (al-munshaʾāt), with which the long vowel cannot meet.]», and the preferred way is to pronounce it in connection. If someone pauses on it without the yāʾ, that is permissible though far-fetched, but he should give a faint hint (rawm) of the kasra on the rāʾ to indicate the omission of the yāʾ. It is also read "اَلْمُنْشِئاتُ", with kasra on the shīn, but fatḥa on the shīn is better. The meaning of "اَلْمُنْشَآتُ" is: those whose sails are raised; and "اَلْمُنْشِئاتُ" is in the sense of those that carry and raise sails. The meaning of "كالأعْلامِ" is: like mountains. The poet said:
؎إذا قَطَعْنَ عَلَمًا بَدا عَلَمْ
(Whenever they cross one mountain, another mountain appears.)
And "اَلْجَوارِي" are the ships.

zajjaj:26-26.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُلُّ مَن عَلَيْها فانٍ﴾: its meaning is: on the earth.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿خَلَقَ الإنْسانَ﴾ ﴿عَلَّمَهُ البَيانَ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 4]: it has been said that by "man" here He means the Prophet ﷺ, and "عَلَّمَهُ البَيانَ" means "He taught him the Qurʾān, in which is the clear explanation of everything". And it has been said: "man" here is Adam ﷺ. And it is permissible in the language for "الإنْسانَ" to be a name for the genus of all people; on this meaning "عَلَّمَهُ البَيانَ" means: He made him discerning, so that man became distinct from all the animals.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿الشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ بِحُسْبانٍ﴾: "اَلشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ" are both nominative as subjects (by ibtidāʾ, the mubtadaʾ).
And His saying ﴿بِحُسْبانٍ﴾ indicates the khabar (predicate) of the subject; the meaning is: "The sun and the moon run by reckoning." And the meaning of ﴿بِحُسْبانٍ﴾ may also be that they both indicate the number of the months and years and all times.

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والنَّجْمُ والشَّجَرُ يَسْجُدانِ﴾: the philologists and most of the exegetes said: "اَلنَّجْمُ" is everything that grows on the face of the earth that has no stalk, and "اَلشَّجَرُ" is everything that has a stalk. The meaning of their prostration is the turning of the shade with them, as He said: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إلى ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِن شَيْءٍ يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلالُهُ عَنِ اليَمِينِ والشَّمائِلِ سُجَّدًا لِلَّهِ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 48]. It has also been said that by al-najm the stars are meant, and this may be so, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has informed us that the stars prostrate, saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ والشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ والنُّجُومُ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 18]. And it may be that by al-najm here He means both what grows on the face of the earth and what rises of the stars of the sky; of everything that rises (ṭalaʿa) one says "qad najama" (it has appeared).

zajjaj:7-7.t: And His saying: ﴿والسَّماءَ رَفَعَها ووَضَعَ المِيزانَ﴾: the meaning is: "He raised it above the earth and held it back from falling onto the earth, and He set up the balance so that people may obtain justice from one another." And it has been said: "اَلْمِيزانُ" here is justice, because equity (al-muʿādala) is the weighing of things against one another.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿ألا تَطْغَوْا في المِيزانِ﴾: that you do not exceed the measure and justice. ﴿ألا تَطْغَوْا﴾ may be in the sense of the lām: "so that you do not transgress"; and ﴿ألا تَطْغَوْا﴾ may be a prohibition, with "أنْ" having the explicative sense (al-tafsīr), so that the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "And He set up the balance", that is: "Do not transgress in the balance." This is indicated by what is conjoined to it, namely His saying: ﴿وَأقِيمُوا الوَزْنَ بِالقِسْطِ ولا تُخْسِرُوا المِيزانَ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 9]. The reading is with ḍamma on the tāʾ. The philologists have transmitted "akhsarta l-mīzāna" and "khasarta" (you made the balance deficient); on "khasarta" it would be "وَلا تَخْسِرُوا". But do not read it so unless a sound transmission from an imam of reading is established. It has been reported that a certain person among the early ones read it so, but he is not one from whom reading was taken, nor does he have a reading (ḥarf) according to which people read.

zajjaj:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿سَنَفْرُغُ لَكم أيُّهَ الثَّقَلانِ﴾: by al-thaqalān (the two weighty ones) He means humans and jinn. "سَنَفْرَغُ لَكُمْ" with fatḥa on the rāʾ is permissible; "سَيَفْرُغُ" with fatḥa on the yāʾ is permissible; and "سَيُفْرَغُ لَكُمْ" with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the rāʾ is permissible. Its meaning is: We shall turn to your reckoning — and Allah is not distracted by one matter from another. Farāgh in the language is of two kinds: one of them is being free from an occupation, and the other is directing oneself to a thing. You say "qad faraghtu mimmā kuntu fīhi" (I have finished with what I was engaged in), that is: my occupation with it has ceased; and you say "sa-atafarraghu li-fulān" (I shall devote myself to So-and-so), that is: I shall make him my aim.

zajjaj:33-33.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا مَعْشَرَ الجِنِّ والإنْسِ إنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ أنْ تَنْفُذُوا مِن أقْطارِ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾: al-aqṭār are the regions. ﴿لا تَنْفُذُونَ إلا بِسُلْطانٍ﴾, that is: wherever you are, you witness a proof and an authority from Allah indicating that He is One.

zajjaj:35-35.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُرْسَلُ عَلَيْكُما شُواظٌ مِن نارٍ ونُحاسٌ﴾, and it is also read "وَنُحاسٍ", with kasra on the sīn. Al-nuḥās is smoke, and al-shuwāẓ is the flame that has no smoke with it.

zajjaj:37-37.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإذا انْشَقَّتِ السَّماءُ فَكانَتْ ورْدَةً كالدِّهانِ﴾: the meaning of ﴿وَرْدَةً﴾ is: it became like the colour of the rose, and that is on the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of ﴿كالدِّهانِ﴾ is: it changes colour from the greatest terror, as the various oils change colour; al-dihān is the plural of "دُهْنٍ" (oil). The evidence for this is His saying ﴿يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السَّماءُ كالمُهْلِ﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 8], that is: like oil that has been boiled. And it has been said: ﴿فَكانَتْ ورْدَةً كالدِّهانِ﴾ means it became like the colour of a ward (bay-red) horse; "al-kumayt" is al-ward, whose colour changes, so that in winter its colour differs from its colour in summer, and in the season [between] its colour is other than its colour in winter and summer «[Translator's note: the bracketed word is added for clarity.]».

zajjaj:39-39.t:
﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُسْألُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إنْسٌ ولا جانٌّ﴾, while He said elsewhere: ﴿وَقِفُوهم إنَّهم مَسْؤُولُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 24]. When that day comes, the mark of the criminals will be blackness of the face and blueness [of the eyes] «[Translator's note: the bracketed words are added for clarity.]». The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿يُعْرَفُ المُجْرِمُونَ بِسِيماهم فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّواصِي والأقْدامِ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 41], that is: by this mark of theirs; and the evidence for that is His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 106].
And His saying: ﴿وَنَحْشُرُ المُجْرِمِينَ يَوْمَئِذٍ زُرْقًا﴾ [Ṭā Hā: 102].

zajjaj:41-41.t: And His saying: ﴿فَيُؤْخَذُ بِالنَّواصِي والأقْدامِ﴾: it has been said: the feet are joined to the forelocks from behind, and they are cast into the Fire; and that is more severe in their punishment and in their disfigurement.

zajjaj:43-44.t: And His saying: ﴿هَذِهِ جَهَنَّمُ الَّتِي يُكَذِّبُ بِها المُجْرِمُونَ﴾ ﴿يَطُوفُونَ بَيْنَها وبَيْنَ حَمِيمٍ آنٍ﴾: ﴿آنٍ﴾ is from "qad aniya, yaʾnā, fa-huwa ānin", when something reaches the utmost in cooking and heat. When they cry for relief from the Fire, their relief is made the boiling water (al-ḥamīm al-ānī) which has become like molten metal (al-muhl); so they are taken round, once to the boiling water and once to the Fire — I seek refuge with Allah and His mercy from it. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known what there is for whoever fears Him and is in awe of Him, saying: ﴿وَلِمَن خافَ مَقامَ رَبِّهِ جَنَّتانِ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 46]. It has been said: whoever intends a sin, then remembers what he will bear for it, and abandons it out of fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, dread of His punishment and hope for His reward, will have two gardens. Then He described them, saying: ﴿ذَواتا أفْنانٍ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 48]. Al-afnān is the plural of "fann" (kind), that is: he will have in them whatever souls desire and eyes delight in, of every kind; so "al-afnān" means the varieties. And "al-afnān" also means the branches, whose singular is "fanan"; and this is the better of the two views.

zajjaj:52-52.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيهِما مِن كُلِّ فاكِهَةٍ زَوْجانِ﴾: "اَلزَّوْجانِ" means the two kinds.

zajjaj:56-56.t:
And His saying: ﴿فِيهِنَّ قاصِراتُ الطَّرْفِ﴾: its meaning is: in them are ḥūr who restrain their glances, who have confined their glances to their husbands and do not look at others.
﴿لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ إنْسٌ قَبْلَهم ولا جانٌّ﴾: no one has touched them. It is also read "لَمْ يَطْمُثْهُنَّ", but that is rare in reading; in the language one says "ṭamatha, yaṭmithu and yaṭmuthu". In this verse there is evidence that the jinnī has intercourse, just as the human has intercourse.

zajjaj:58-58.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَأنَّهُنَّ الياقُوتُ والمَرْجانُ﴾: the exegetes and the philologists said: they are in the clarity of rubies and the whiteness of marjān; al-marjān is small pearls, and it is whiter.
And His saying: ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 56] — while He mentioned only two gardens — means: in these two gardens and what has been prepared for the person in this account besides these two gardens.

zajjaj:60-60.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَلْ جَزاءُ الإحْسانِ إلا الإحْسانُ﴾, that is: the recompense of one who did good in this world is nothing but that good be done to him in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:62-62.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن دُونِهِما جَنَّتانِ﴾, that is: for whoever fears the standing before his Lord there are two gardens, and besides them he has two [more] gardens «[Translator's note: the bracketed word is added for clarity.]». "اَلْجَنَّةُ" in the language of the Arabs is the orchard.

zajjaj:64-64.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُدْهامَّتانِ﴾: meaning that they are both green, their greenness verging on black. With every green plant, the fullness of its greenness and its being well-watered is that it verges on black.

zajjaj:66-66.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيهِما عَيْنانِ نَضّاخَتانِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that they both gush forth every good thing.

zajjaj:68-68.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيهِما فاكِهَةٌ ونَخْلٌ ورُمّانٌ﴾: some people said that palm trees and pomegranates are not among fruit. But some of the philologists — among them Yūnus the grammarian, who comes next after al-Khalīl in seniority and skill — said that pomegranates and palms are among the most excellent of fruit, and they were separated by the wāw only because of their excellence. He cited as evidence for that His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿مَن كانَ عَدُوًّا لِلَّهِ ومَلائِكَتِهِ ورُسُلِهِ وجِبْرِيلَ ومِيكالَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 98], and said: because of their excellence they were separated by the wāw.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلى فُرُشٍ بَطائِنُها مِن إسْتَبْرَقٍ وجَنى الجَنَّتَيْنِ دانٍ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 54]: it has been said: "اَلْإسْتَبْرَقُ" is very thick brocade, like what is made for the Kaʿba; and "اَلْبَطائِنُ" (the linings) are what is next to the ground.
And His saying: ﴿وَجَنى الجَنَّتَيْنِ دانٍ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 54], that is: what is picked of their fruit, when they want it, comes near to their mouths, so that they take it with their mouths and hands.

zajjaj:70-70.t: And His saying: ﴿فِيهِنَّ خَيْراتٌ حِسانٌ﴾: its origin in the language is "خَيِّراتٌ", and the meaning is that they are good in character and beautiful in form. It has been read so — I mean with a doubled yāʾ.

zajjaj:72-72.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حُورٌ مَقْصُوراتٌ في الخِيامِ﴾: "اَلْخِيامُ" in the language of the Arabs is the plural of khayma (tent). And "al-khiyām" are two things: al-khiyām are the camel-litters (hawādij), and al-khiyām are the dwellings. It has come in the exegesis that each tent of these tents is of a hollowed pearl. The meaning of ﴿مَقْصُوراتٌ﴾ is: secluded, confined to their husbands.

zajjaj:76-76.t:
And His saying: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلى رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ وعَبْقَرِيٍّ حِسانٍ﴾, and it has also been read "عَلى رَفارِفَ خُضْرٍ وعَباقِرِيَّ حِسانٍ". The reading is the first one; this reading has no justification in Arabic, because a plural with two letters after its alif, like "مَساجِدُ" and "مَفاتِيحُ", does not admit a form like "عَباقِرِيَّ", since what exceeds three letters is not pluralised with the yāʾ of relation (yāʾ al-nisba). If you pluralised "عَبْقَرِيٌّ", its plural would be "عَباقِرَةٌ", just as if you pluralised "مُهَلَّبِيٌّ" its plural would be "مَهالِبَةٌ" — one does not say "مَهالِبِيُّ".
If someone asks: how then is "عَبْقَرِيٍّ حِسانٍ" permissible, when "عَبْقَرِيٍّ" is singular and "حِسانٌ" is plural? The basis is that its singular is "عَبْقَرِيَّةٌ" and the plural (collective) is "عَبْقَرِيٌّ", as you say "ثَمَرَةٌ" and "ثَمَرٌ", "لَوْزَةٌ" and "لَوْزٌ"; and "عَبْقَرِيٌّ" may also be a generic noun. So the reading is the first one.
As for the explanation of ﴿رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ وعَبْقَرِيٍّ﴾: they said al-rafraf here is the meadows of Paradise; they said al-rafraf is cushions; they said it is maḥābis (covers); and they also said it is the overhanging parts of the covers of the furnishings. As for al-ʿabqarī, they said it is carpets, and they said it is spread-out rugs (ṭanāfis). What indicates this in the Qurʾān is His saying: ﴿وَنَمارِقُ مَصْفُوفَةٌ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 15] ﴿وَزَرابِيُّ مَبْثُوثَةٌ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 16]: al-namāriq are cushions and al-zarābī are carpets. So the meaning of "رَفْرَفٍ" here and "عَبْقَرِيٍّ" is cushions and carpets; and it indicates — and Allah knows best — that the cushions have fringes (rafraf). The origin of "اَلْعَبْقَرِيُّ" in the language is a description of everything whose description is carried to the extreme. Its origin is that "ʿAbqar" was the name of a land in which carpets and other things were embroidered, so every excellent thing, and everything whose description is carried to the extreme, was attributed to "ʿAbqar". Zuhayr said:
؎بِخَيْلٍ عَلَيْها جِنَّةٌ عَبْقَرِيَّةٌ ∗∗∗ جَدِيرُونَ يَوْمًا أنْ يَنالُوا فَيَسْتَعْلُوا
(With horses bearing riders like the jinn of ʿAbqar, worthy one day to attain [their aim] and prevail.)

zajjaj:77-77.t: And His saying: ﴿فَبِأيِّ آلاءِ رَبِّكُما تُكَذِّبانِ﴾, that is: which of the favours of your Lord that have been enumerated to you, O company of jinn and humans, do you both deny? Rather, you ought to glorify Allah and extol Him. So He closed the surah with that by which He, Mighty and Majestic is He, ought to be extolled and glorified, saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَبارَكَ اسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِي الجَلالِ والإكْرامِ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 78].
